text: Create a new Python project with the uv init command
quote: You can create a new Python project using the `uv init` command

text: Add dependencies to pyproject.toml via uv add, which also updates the lockfile and project environment
quote: You can add dependencies to your `pyproject.toml` with the `uv add` command. This will also update the lockfile and project environment

text: Remove a dependency from the project with uv remove
quote: To remove a package, you can use `uv remove`

text: Upgrade one package to its latest compatible version with --upgrade-package while keeping the rest of the lockfile intact
quote: The `--upgrade-package` flag will attempt to update the specified package to the latest compatible version, while keeping the rest of the lockfile intact.

text: Specify version constraints or alternative sources when adding dependencies
quote: You can also specify version constraints or alternative sources

text: Migrate from a requirements.txt file by adding all of its dependencies with uv add -r
quote: If you're migrating from a `requirements.txt` file, you can use `uv add` with the `-r` flag to add all dependencies from the file

text: Run scripts, with support for inline dependency metadata
quote: Runs scripts, with support for inline dependency metadata.

text: Manage dependencies and environments for single-file scripts
quote: uv manages dependencies and environments for single-file scripts.

text: Add dependencies to a script's inline metadata with uv add --script
quote:
$ uv add --script example.py requests
Updated `example.py`

text: A single tool meant to replace pip, pip-tools, pipx, poetry, pyenv, twine, virtualenv, and more
quote: A single tool to replace `pip`, `pip-tools`, `pipx`, `poetry`, `pyenv`, `twine`, `virtualenv`, and more.

text: Provides a drop-in replacement for common pip, pip-tools, and virtualenv commands through the uv pip interface
quote: uv provides a drop-in replacement for common `pip`, `pip-tools`, and `virtualenv` commands.

text: Install Python versions and switch between them quickly
quote: uv installs Python and allows quickly switching between versions.

text: Download Python versions automatically as needed
quote: Download Python versions as needed

text: Pin a project's Python version to a .python-version file with uv python pin
quote:
Use a specific Python version in the current directory:

console
$ uv python pin 3.11
Pinned `.python-version` to `3.11`

text: Respect the Python version pinned in the project
quote: This will respect the Python version pinned in the project.

text: Create a virtual environment with a specific Python version using uv venv --python
quote:
$ uv venv --python 3.12.0
Using CPython 3.12.0
Creating virtual environment at: .venv

text: Run tools without installing them using uvx / uv tool run, in a temporary environment isolated from the project
quote: Tools can be invoked without installation using `uv tool run`, in which case their dependencies are installed in a temporary virtual environment isolated from the current project.

text: Install tools with uv tool install so their executables are available on PATH
quote: Tools can also be installed with `uv tool install`, in which case their executables are available on the `PATH`

text: Run a specific tool version with uvx tool@version
quote:
For example, to run a specific version of Ruff:

$ uvx [email protected] --version
ruff 0.6.0

text: Include extra packages when running a tool with uvx --with
quote:
Additional packages can be included during tool execution:

`$ uvx --with <extra-package> <tool>`

text: uv tool install accepts package@version and package@latest specifiers
quote: `uv tool install` will also respect the `{package}@{version}` and `{package}@latest` specifiers

text: Upgrade tool environments with uv tool upgrade, or re-create them with uv tool install
quote: Tool environments may be upgraded via `uv tool upgrade`, or re-created entirely via subsequent `uv tool install` operations.

text: Tool upgrades respect the version constraints given when the tool was installed
quote: Tool upgrades will respect the version constraints provided when installing the tool.

text: Run commands in the project environment with uv run
quote:
$ uv run ruff check
All checks passed!

text: uv.lock is a cross-platform lockfile that records exact information about project dependencies
quote: `uv.lock` is a cross-platform lockfile that contains exact information about your project's dependencies.

text: Supports Cargo-style workspaces for scalable projects
quote: Supports Cargo-style [workspaces](concepts/projects/workspaces/) for scalable projects.

text: Official astral-sh/setup-uv GitHub Action installs uv, adds it to PATH, and can persist the cache
quote: we recommend the official `astral-sh/setup-uv` action, which installs uv, adds it to PATH, (optionally) persists the cache, and more

text: Set the Python version for CI matrix testing through astral-sh/setup-uv
quote: When using a matrix to test multiple Python versions, set the Python version using `astral-sh/setup-uv`

text: Uses aggressive caching to avoid re-downloading and re-building dependencies already accessed in prior runs
quote: uv uses aggressive caching to avoid re-downloading (and re-building) dependencies that have already been accessed in prior runs.

text: Disk-space efficient global cache that deduplicates dependencies
quote: Disk-space efficient, with a [global cache](concepts/cache/) for dependency deduplication.

text: Configure custom cache keys under tool.uv.cache-keys, covering file paths and Git commit hashes
quote: you can add cache key entries under `tool.uv.cache-keys`, which covers both file paths and Git commit hashes.

text: Clear the whole cache or the cache for one package with uv cache clean
quote: To clear the cache entirely, run `uv cache clean`. To clear the cache for a specific package, run `uv cache clean <package-name>`.

text: Force revalidation of cached data for all dependencies by passing --refresh to any command
quote: To force uv to revalidate cached data for all dependencies, pass `--refresh` to any command

text: Self-update to the latest version with uv self update when installed via the standalone installer
quote: When uv is installed via the standalone installer, it can update itself on-demand: `uv self update`

text: Shell autocompletion for uv commands
quote: To enable shell autocompletion for uv commands, run one of the following:

text: Read the package version with uv version
quote: The `uv version` command can be used to read your package's version.

text: uv version supports JSON output via --output-format json
quote: $ uv version --output-format json

text: Build and publish projects, including ones not managed with uv
quote: uv also supports building and publishing projects, even if they're not managed with uv.

text: Installable without Rust or Python, via curl or pip
quote: Installable without Rust or Python via `curl` or `pip`.

text: Install via standalone installers or a package manager of your choice
quote: Install uv with our standalone installers or your package manager of choice.

text: Supports macOS, Linux, and Windows
quote: Supports macOS, Linux, and Windows.

text: Claims to be 10-100x faster than pip
quote: 10-100x faster than `pip`.

text: Publishes an llms.txt documentation index, and every docs page is fetchable as raw markdown
quote: uv publishes an llms.txt index of its documentation at docs.astral.sh/uv/llms.txt (served as text/plain): "# uv > uv is an extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust." — every docs page is also fetchable as raw markd
